title: Online shop insurance in Moldova: stock, payments and deliveries

content:
An online shop faces different risks before, during and after delivery. Warehouse stock, a damaged parcel, a disputed payment and a data breach are not the same event. For an insurance assessment of an online shop in Moldova, describe each stage and who is responsible for it.

This material helps retailers selling through their own websites, platforms or social networks. It does not confirm the existence of one policy covering every operation. Available products, property, contracts and accepted conditions must be checked before a quotation. Examples are preparation scenarios, not real ING Broker client cases.

Follow the product's physical journey

Trace a product from receipt from the supplier to receipt by the buyer. Include storage, packing, handover to the courier and any return. For each stage, record the location, document and responsible party. An accurate list of addresses is more useful than saying the business operates exclusively online.

Declare whether goods are kept at home, in a rented warehouse or with a logistics partner. Do not assume a home policy includes commercial stock. A lease also does not establish that your goods are insured. The building owner and goods owner may have different interests.

Make stock values explainable

Prepare product categories, purchase documents and the method used to record quantities. Separate your own goods from consignment stock or another seller's property. For returns, identify resalable products and items awaiting examination. These differences matter to the inventory submitted for assessment.

Explain seasonal changes in stock and where overflow is stored. Do not automatically use a normal month's value for a busy period. Photographs of shelves do not replace valuation records. Ask which valuation method is accepted and how inventory changes during the contract are handled.

Packing and handover are separate checks

Describe packaging for fragile, electronic or temperature-sensitive products where relevant. Do not describe packaging as compliant with a requirement you have not checked. Request the applicable conditions for the category being transported and keep instructions from the partners involved.

At parcel handover, track the document, shipment number, quantity and recorded condition. Proof that a parcel was collected is different from proof that its contents were complete and correctly packed. Decide who keeps useful photographs and how long authorized people can access them.

A courier is not automatically your goods insurer

Read the delivery company's contract and complaints procedure. Declared value, carrier liability and any goods insurance need separate explanations. Do not assume a delivery fee includes full compensation for every lost or damaged parcel. Request a written explanation of the actual service.

For your own deliveries, record vehicles, routes, stops and how goods are kept in the vehicle. Motor insurance should not be interpreted as automatic protection for every parcel. If several partners are used, compare responsibilities for the same stage, not only advertised delivery speed.

Returns have their own risk journey

A returned item may be transported, received and inspected by different people from those involved in its original dispatch. Define how the order is identified and the product's condition recorded. Keep the commercial reason for a return separate from findings of damage. A dissatisfied customer does not automatically create an insured loss.

The shop's return policy and legal duties require separate review by the appropriate specialist. This article sets no universal consumer deadlines. For risk assessment, explain the actual process and the business's costs without assuming insurance will take over every expense.

Online payment and delivery are different processes

Describe actual payment channels: processor, transfer, cash on delivery or others. Who keeps transaction records? How are orders reconciled with money received? Do not send card details, integration keys or processor-account access for an insurance conversation.

A disputed payment, fraudulent order and integration error can have different causes and procedures. Read the processor's responsibilities in its contract. Cyber insurance must not be presented as protection against every payment refusal. Ask about the specific situation and request an answer linked to the proposal's conditions.

Protect access to the shop and domain

The administration account, domain and email address may be controlled by different people or businesses. List account holders and recovery procedures. Use available authentication measures and individual access appropriate to each role. A technical provider should know what it may change and who approves significant changes.

With the technical team, check what can be restored after a problem: catalogue, orders, files and configuration. A copy of product images is not necessarily a backup of the entire shop. Initially describe those functions without attaching customer databases or revealing sensitive configurations.

Assess impact without invented figures

Separate orders that could be taken through another channel from orders actually lost. Record additional packing, space, staffing and communication costs. The value of abandoned baskets does not automatically establish a revenue loss. Use business records and explain assumptions behind internal estimates.

If you want a business interruption assessment, ask which event and loss might be accepted. Paid advertising, unsuccessful promotion or a seasonal sales decline do not automatically become insured risks. Responsible comparison separates proposed costs, excluded costs and points still awaiting confirmation.

A hypothetical damaged-parcel review

Imagine a fragile product arriving damaged. Trace warehouse receipt, packing, courier handover and the finding at destination in sequence. Do not determine the cause from the final photograph alone. Identify records for each stage and missing information. This example does not establish courier liability or cover under a particular policy.

Maintain the link between product, order and shipment without publishing the customer's address or personal data. If packaging matters to an inspection, request instructions before discarding it. Separate the commercial solution offered to the buyer from a later insurance review. Replacing the product to preserve the relationship does not establish that the insurer accepts that cost.

Also retain the delivery-contract version applying to that order. A procedure changed later does not automatically explain obligations on the dispatch date. Record when instructions arrived and who confirmed their adoption in the shop's process.

Check promises in product descriptions

The catalogue should match delivered goods, including stated features and uses. For products with instructions or special requirements, keep supplier documents and verify explanations with the appropriate specialist. Do not invent certifications, compatibility or warranties. An exaggerated sales promise may lead to a complaint different from physical damage during transport.

Describe own-brand, imported or modified products in the activity assessment. The retailer's role and responsibilities require legal review for the particular category. Stock insurance does not automatically include product liability or the cost of recalling items from customers. Discuss those questions separately rather than filling a form with assumptions.

Reconcile campaigns, orders and stock

Before a campaign, check where goods are located and who updates availability. An inventory error can generate orders for unavailable products. That is not automatically an insured loss. Establish who can stop selling an item and how accepted orders are identified without hidden changes to their history.

Separate cancellations for missing stock, commercial returns and transport incidents in internal records. This classification improves operations and helps explain an event. Do not present all cancelled orders as insurance losses. If using an estimate, state its method and underlying records rather than selecting a percentage to make the request look larger.

A retailer's preparation sheet

A useful summary covers products, locations, goods owners, delivery methods and digital providers. Attach only documents requested for that stage. Full contracts, customer data and payment information should not be sent through a public form. First agree the purpose, recipient and suitable channel for confidential material.

  • Documented inventory and seasonal changes.
  • Actual storage addresses and temporary premises.
  • Goods categories and packaging methods.
  • Delivery contracts and return routes.
  • Access to the shop, domain and saved orders.
  • Separate questions about property, transport, liability and cyber risks.

Check that a proposal describes your actual business. Do not compare it with another type of shop or a package published in another country. Ask for unconfirmed conditions to be marked and keep written answers. When adding a product category or changing warehouse, request a review before relying on old explanations.

Frequently asked questions about e-commerce insurance

Does one policy include the website, stock and every return?

Do not infer this from the term e-commerce. Assess property, transport, liability and digital risks separately. Availability needs confirmation for the actual business.

Is the courier's insurance enough?

Read the delivery contract, limits and applicable procedure. A partner's insurance does not establish full protection for your stock or every parcel.

What should I send before discussing insurance?

Describe products, premises, documented values, delivery processes and digital services. Send only requested documents through the agreed channel. Do not share passwords, card details or customer databases.

Risk acceptance, conditions and claims handling belong to the insurer under the contract. This article does not confirm product availability or coverage of an individual case.
